summary: NIH RePORTER returns one record per support year rather than one per project, so any listing that treats a row as an award repeats the same grant many times: the response struct must request core_project_num, the client must over-fetch and dedup on it keeping the highest-amount support year, and every user-facing count must be described as award records rather than awards.
reason: Measured on 100 records the API returned 71 distinct projects, and core project 5R01CA092447 alone occupied 11 rows; in the top 15 rows sorted by award amount only 7 distinct projects were present, so the size-sorted listing a user actually reads was more than half duplicates. Truncating the full project number is not a valid dedup key: observed forms 5R01CA092447-08, 2R01CA092447-06A1 and 3R01CA092447-08S1 vary in both the leading application-type digit and the suffix length, so no fixed-width truncation works. The API already returns core_project_num; it was simply missing from the response struct. A regen that drops that field, removes the over-fetch factor, or restores wording that calls the API total 'matching awards' silently reintroduces a listing whose row count and typical-award population are support years misreported as distinct grants.
validated_outcome: With core_project_num requested, nihOverFetch = 6 and dedup keeping the highest-amount support year per core project, a 15-row listing went from 7 distinct projects to 15 distinct projects.
